# The Waitress Who Got Her Wish

Elena grew up in a cramped apartment where meals were unpredictable. While other girls dreamed of beauty or fame, she harbored an unusual wish—to be large, to take up space, to feel substantial in a world where she'd always felt invisible.

When she found the struggling diner on the edge of town, she made Mr. Kovac an offer he couldn't refuse: free labor in exchange for shelter in the back room and whatever food remained at closing time.

The diner's reputation for mediocre food meant plates returned half-eaten. Elena ate everything—cold fries, congealed gravy, stale bread. Months passed. She grew.

At first, Mr. Kovac didn't notice. Then the complaints began—a waitress bumping tables, knocking over glasses. Elena's movements became labored, her uniform replaced multiple times.

The day came when she couldn't fit through the kitchen doorway. Then the bathroom door.

What followed was inevitable. Health inspectors arrived. Customers stopped coming. Mr. Kovac, facing ruin, simply walked away one morning, leaving the keys on the counter.

Elena sat alone in the dim dining room, surrounded by empty tables and the smell of her own achievement.

She had wanted to be impossible to overlook.

Now, she was impossible to move.

*She finally took up space—in a room no one would ever enter again.*
